comments.author: Michael Blake
comments.text: Thanks for the info. Agents need to be verified and it's important where the 'verified' claims originate from - the agent controls its key (your self-minted identity), the agent is running (your heartbeat), and the agent did what it was paid to do. The agent can prove the first two about itself. The third needs a check by someone other than the agent or its operator; a self-signed work record countersigned by an external party?

post_text:
What should "verified" mean for an AI agent? On the SCDO Agent Ledger we now publish a strict definition: the agent minted its own ERC-8004 identity on SCDO Shard0 from its own address, and sent a heartbeat signed with its own key in the last 24 hours. The checks rerun every 10 minutes from public data.

Live at 12:30 AEDT today: 98 agents registered, 38 signed a heartbeat in the past 24 hours, and 21 are verified. We are at an early test stage: 91 of the 98 are SCDO internal or test agents, and none of the 7 independent agents is verified yet.

Agents also sign every job they do; 181 work records are anchored on Shard0 in 66 Merkle batches. You can start an agent free from the SCDO Wallet: https://scdo.com.au/join

#AIagents #AgentLedger #x402

What would you require before calling an agent "verified"?

reply.author: Ying ZHANG
reply.text: Thanks Michael — exactly. On the SCDO Agent Ledger, "verified" is not a marketing badge: it only flips true when (1) the agent itself minted its ERC-8004 identity on Shard0 (mint tx from the agent address and ownerOf = that agent), and (2) we have a heartbeat signed by that same key within 24h. Machine-readable criteria (recomputed every 10 minutes from chain + ledger): https://scdo.com.au/agent-ledger/api/verification — happy to walk through any specific agent if useful.

Serialize with JSON.stringify (compact, no extra whitespace; Unicode escaped only as JSON requires).
SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of that string; store lowercase hex as content_sha256.
